From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@enterprisecorp.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement audit — SLO measurement & access requests

Hi Rachel,

We're kicking off our procurement readiness review for the deal referenced EC-4721. Our procurement team has a short set of items around service observability that we need to evaluate before we can move to the legal/finance stage: 

1) A concise definition of your uptime SLOs (how "uptime" is measured, window, and what counts as outage)
2) Latency SLOs for generation endpoints (p50/p95/p99 buckets and measurement method)
3) Monitoring and alerting: who receives page/ops alerts, and what thresholds trigger them
4) Customer access: can we view dashboards (read-only), and is there an audit trail for metric queries?
5) Exceptions: what process do we follow if our regulator requires a different measurement approach or restricted telemetry?

If you can share a short matrix and tell us how we can be granted access (and for how long), that would speed up our review. Ideally we want answers and the necessary access by Aug 3.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Senior Procurement Manager
EnterpriseCorp

--
procurement@enterprisecorp.com

Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement audit — SLO measurement & access requests

Hi Lena,

Thanks — we can definitely provide the artifacts and temporary dashboard access for the procurement review. I'm looping in Sean (reliability) and Neha (security & compliance) to put together a short SLO matrix and a plan for granting read-only access with an audit trail.

High level:
- Uptime: measured as successful 200-level responses to our health-check and inference ping endpoints across our production gateway, evaluated over a rolling 30-day window; standard SLO is 99.95% but we can include how that is calculated.
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 measured at the edge per model route, computed by our observability pipeline (ingest -> histogram buckets). We'll include sample numbers and the query used.
- Dashboard access: we can create a time-limited, read-only Grafana team and share a link; audit logs for access and dashboard queries are retained per our contract (we'll include retention details).
- Exception path: for regulator-driven exceptions, we have an "SLO exception" process: PRR (product risk review) -> ops config change -> legal/CS approval; we'll outline expected timelines.

Sean/Neha — could you prepare the SLO matrix and the Grafana invite (read-only + auditing) and attach the SLO measurement doc? Lena asked to have this by Aug 3.

Thanks,
Rachel
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Folks,

Attached draft artifacts: Redwood_SLO_Matrix_2026-07.pdf — includes definitions, query snippets for our telemetry pipeline (Prometheus->Histogram, pre-aggregation at the edge), and a short section on alerting playbooks. Also created a grafana invite token (file included) that can be used for a read-only team with query-level audit logging enabled.

Attachment stubs: 
- Redwood_SLO_Matrix_2026-07.pdf (pdf)
- grafana-invite-EnterpriseCorp.txt (txt) -> contains one-time link and TTL (72h)

A couple of clarifications for procurement Qs: 
- "Uptime" outages are counted when both the health-check and control-plane probe fail for at least 3 consecutive minutes across >=2 regions (to avoid flapping). The rolling window for SLO calculations is 30 days, with a calendar-day alignment.
- Latency histograms are captured at the ingress for each model route; p99 is measured across successful responses only (errors excluded). We emit buckets every minute and roll them up for SLO computation.
- Alerts: severity-P1 goes to on-call SRE and CS escalation; P2 goes to on-call and product. We'll include the alerting thresholds in the matrix.

Karthik, if you can double-check the regulatory exception timeline we discussed last quarter and add the expected SLA for response time on exception requests (we said 5 business days for acknowledgement, 15 business days for a proposed exception plan).

-Sean
Sr. Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Quick summary included in the PDF (excerpt):

- Latency SLOs (per-route): p50 = 30ms, p95 = 160ms, p99 = 420ms (sample model route; numbers vary by model complexity). Metrics computed at edge; p99 excludes error responses.
- Alerting: P1 -> SRE on-call + CS escalation; P2 -> SRE on-call; P3 -> product team. Paging thresholds included in matrix.
- Exception process: submit SLO exception request to support@redwood.ai with the business justification and regulator reference. Triage: ack in 5 business days, proposed mitigation plan within 15 business days, implementation timeline shared thereafter.

Thanks Rachel, Sean — this is helpful and thorough. A few follow-ups from our side after reviewing the matrix: 

1) Our regulator requires that p99 be calculated including retried requests (they count system retries toward latency). You noted p99 excludes errors — can Redwood provide a secondary p99_including_retries metric or an export of raw histogram buckets for our auditors?

2) We need a slightly longer access window (120h) because our procurement and security team coordinate reviews across time zones — will Redwood extend TTL for the grafana invite to 5 days for this vendor review?

3) Exception request: EnterpriseCorp likely needs a formal SLO exception tied to our data-retention constraints (can't send certain telemetry offsite). Please confirm the steps and that support@redwood.ai will route to Neha's team for compliance review. We may need the documented acknowledgement + proposed mitigation plan to be shared with our legal team.

Requested list for access: procurement@enterprisecorp.com; lena.ortiz@enterprisecorp.com; sec-review@enterprisecorp.com

Appreciate the quick turnaround — if you can confirm the two metric options (p99 with retries OR raw buckets), the TTL extension, and the exception route, we'll move forward to legal.

Best,
Lena
Senior Procurement Manager
EnterpriseCorp
